dependencies.label: Water Withdrawal & Consumption
dependencies.description: Operational or value-chain reliance on freshwater supplies, including direct withdrawal and consumptive use. Critical where operations are located in water-stressed regions or where large volumes are needed in production.
indicators: Water intensity (m³ per unit of production)
sources: SASB Water Management topic (EM-EP-140a, EM-MM-140a, FB-AG-140a)
TNFD v1.0 — Annex 4.2: Freshwater (provisioning ecosystem services)
Natural Capital Protocol Toolkit (Capital Coalition) — Freshwater module
GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018
IPCC AR6 WGII Ch.4 — Water: global freshwater scarcity projections

dependencies.label: Water Quality & Effluent Management
dependencies.description: Dependency on clean water for operations and risk of discharging pollutants into water bodies. Includes wastewater treatment and compliance with discharge standards.
indicators: % of wastewater treated to tertiary standard
sources: SASB Water Management topic — Effluent quality disclosures
TNFD v1.0 — Regulating services: Water purification & waste treatment
GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018 (GRI 303-4 Water discharge)
EU Water Framework Directive 2000/60/EC — Good ecological status targets
UK Environment Act 2021 — Statutory water quality targets

dependencies.label: Greenhouse Gas Emissions
dependencies.description: Dependency on the atmosphere as a carbon sink. High GHG emitters face transition risk (carbon pricing, regulation) and contribute to physical climate risk for all sectors. Covers Scope 1, 2, and material Scope 3.
sources: SASB GHG Emissions topic (EM-EP-110a, IF-EU-110a, TR-AU-110a)
TCFD Recommendations 2017 (updated 2021) — Transition risk metrics
GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard (WRI/WBCSD 2004)
IPCC AR6 WGI 2021 — Physical Science Basis (1.5°C carbon budgets)
ESRS E1 Climate Change — Paragraphs 40–62 (GHG inventory requirements)

dependencies.label: Air Quality & Local Pollutants
dependencies.description: Release of NOₓ, SOₓ, particulate matter, and volatile organic compounds affecting local air quality. Subject to regulatory limits and community health concerns.
sources: SASB Air Quality topic (EM-EP-120a, EM-IS-120a, TR-AU-120a)
ESRS E2 Pollution — AR 8–12 (air pollutant emissions to air)
GRI 305: Emissions 2016 (GRI 305-6 NOx, SOx, significant air emissions)
UK Environment Act 2021 — PM2.5 and NO2 concentration targets
WHO Global Air Quality Guidelines 2021

dependencies.label: Land Use, Degradation & Contamination
dependencies.description: Physical footprint of operations, land conversion, soil degradation and contamination. Includes remediation liabilities from historical contamination. Material for extractives, agriculture, and development sectors.
sources: SASB Ecological Impacts topic (EM-EP-160a, EM-MM-160a)
TNFD v1.0 — Pillar 3 (Dependencies): Terrestrial ecosystem services
ESRS E4 Biodiversity — Paragraphs 14–22 (land-use change, contamination)
IPBES Land Degradation Assessment 2018 — Global synthesis
GRI 304: Biodiversity 2016 (GRI 304-1 Sites in/near protected areas)

dependencies.label: Soil Health & Fertility
dependencies.description: Dependency on fertile, structurally sound soils for agricultural production, landscaping, or as a building substrate. Covers erosion, compaction, nutrient depletion, and soil carbon.
dependencies.tnfd_ecosystem_service: Provisioning – Soil Fertility; Regulating – Erosion Control
indicators: % of supply-chain land under sustainable agricultural practice
sources: FAO Voluntary Guidelines for Sustainable Soil Management 2017
TNFD v1.0 — Regulating services: Erosion control & soil fertility
ESRS E4 Biodiversity — soil ecosystem integrity indicators
Natural Capital Protocol Toolkit — Soils and Land chapter
EU Soil Health Law (proposed 2023) — soil monitoring framework

dependencies.label: Biodiversity & Habitat
dependencies.description: Reliance on healthy ecosystems for pollination, pest control, coastal protection, and other services underpinning operations or supply chains. Operations in or near sensitive biodiversity areas face regulatory and reputational risk.
dependencies.tnfd_ecosystem_service: Regulating – Pollination, Pest Control, Coastal Protection
indicators: Area of operations in/adjacent to protected areas (ha)
Biodiversity Management Plans in place for sensitive sites
% of supply chain from biodiversity-sensitive regions
sources: TNFD v1.0 — Pillar 4 (Impacts & Dependencies): Biodiversity loss
Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework 2022 — Target 15 (corporate disclosure)
ESRS E4 Biodiversity — Paragraphs 7–13 & Appendix A (material impacts)
IPBES Global Assessment 2019 — 1 million species threatened
SASB Biodiversity Impacts topic (EM-MM-160a, RR-FO-160a)

dependencies.label: Species & Ecosystem Services Dependency
dependencies.description: Value-chain reliance on specific species or ecosystem services (e.g., wild fish stocks, wild pollinators, mangrove coastal protection). Loss of these services creates physical risk to operations.
dependencies.tnfd_ecosystem_service: Provisioning – Wild Fish, Genetic Resources; Cultural – Eco-tourism
indicators: Supply-chain species with IUCN Red List status
Wild-caught fish sourced from MSC-certified fisheries (%)
sources: TNFD v1.0 — Annex 4.3: Regulating & cultural ecosystem services
IPBES Global Assessment 2019 — Ecosystem function decline
Natural Capital Protocol Toolkit (Capital Coalition) — Ecosystem services valuation
MSC, FSC, RSPO certification standards — supply chain biodiversity
ESRS E4 Biodiversity — species and ecosystem condition metrics

dependencies.label: Physical Climate Risk Exposure
dependencies.description: Exposure of assets, supply chains, and operations to chronic (temperature, sea-level rise) and acute (flooding, extreme heat, storms) physical climate hazards. Relevant across all sectors; highest where physical assets are long-lived or located in hazard zones.
indicators: % of assets in high physical-risk locations
Financial exposure to physical climate hazards (£)
sources: TCFD Recommendations 2017 — Physical risk: chronic and acute hazards
IPCC AR6 WGII 2022 — Ch.16: Key risks across sectors and regions
ESRS E1 Climate Change — Paragraphs 63–79 (physical risk exposure)
Bank of England CBES 2021 — Climate Biennial Exploratory Scenario
NGFS (Network for Greening the Financial System) — Physical risk scenarios

dependencies.label: Non-renewable Resource Extraction & Depletion
dependencies.description: Dependency on finite mineral, fossil-fuel, and aggregates resources. Includes supply security, price volatility, and depletion risk as ore grades decline.
indicators: Years of resource reserves at current production
sources: SASB Reserve Quantity & Quality topic (EM-EP-420a)
ESRS E5 Resource Use and Circular Economy — mineral & fossil fuel extraction
IEA World Energy Outlook 2023 — Resource depletion trajectories
Natural Capital Protocol Toolkit — Mineral & fossil resource module
IASB IFRS 6 — Exploration for and Evaluation of Mineral Resources

dependencies.label: Renewable & Bio-based Raw Materials
dependencies.description: Dependency on sustainably sourced biological materials including timber, fibres, agricultural commodities, and marine resources. Overexploitation undermines long-term supply.
indicators: % of key commodities certified sustainable (FSC, RSPO, MSC, etc.)
% of bio-based inputs traceable to source
sources: SASB Supply Chain Management topic (RR-FO, FB-AG, CG-HP)
ESRS E5 Resource Use — Paragraphs 11–18 (biotic resource flows)
FSC Principles & Criteria for Forest Stewardship (FSC-STD-01-001)
RSPO Principles and Criteria 2018 — Sustainable palm oil
EU Regulation on Deforestation-free Products 2023 (EUDR)

dependencies.label: Critical Minerals & Conflict-Sensitive Resources
dependencies.description: Dependency on critical minerals (lithium, cobalt, rare earths) and resources extracted in conflict-affected or high-risk areas. Includes supply security, geopolitical risk, and human rights exposure.
indicators: % of critical minerals sourced from OECD Due Diligence compliant suppliers
Number of 3TG smelters in supply chain audited
sources: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible Mineral Supply Chains 2016
EU Critical Raw Materials Act 2023 — strategic and critical minerals list
ESRS E5 Resource Use — critical material sourcing disclosures
SEC Conflict Minerals Rule (Dodd-Frank §1502) — 3TG minerals
IFC Performance Standard 1 — supply chain risk assessment

dependencies.label: Waste & Hazardous Materials Management
dependencies.description: Generation of hazardous and non-hazardous waste requiring safe disposal or treatment. Includes tailings, chemical waste, and electronic waste. Regulatory and liability exposure where waste is mismanaged.
indicators: Total non-hazardous waste sent to landfill
sources: SASB Waste & Hazardous Materials Management topic (EM-MM-150a, RT-CH-150a)
ESRS E2 Pollution — Paragraphs 13–21 (substances of concern, waste)
GRI 306: Waste 2020 (GRI 306-3 Waste generated, 306-4 Waste diverted)
EU Waste Framework Directive 2008/98/EC — waste hierarchy
UK Environmental Permitting Regulations 2016

dependencies.label: Energy Consumption & Mix
dependencies.description: Dependency on energy (particularly fossil-fuel-derived) for operations. High energy intensity creates cost exposure, transition risk, and GHG emissions. Energy mix (% renewable) drives decarbonisation trajectory.
indicators: Energy intensity (GJ per unit of production or £m revenue)
sources: SASB Energy Management topic (EM-EP-130a, IF-EU-130a, RT-CH-130a)
ESRS E1 Climate Change — Paragraphs 43–45 (energy consumption & mix)
GRI 302: Energy 2016 (GRI 302-1 Energy consumption within the organisation)
IEA Energy Efficiency 2023 — sector-level intensity benchmarks
UK Streamlined Energy and Carbon Reporting (SECR) — mandatory from 2019
